name: One-Pan Sloppy Joe Casserole

ingredients.buy: 1/2 cup plus 1 Tbsp apple cider vinegar
9 bell peppers, diced (about half red, half green)

prose.intro_html:
The sloppy joe was the hero of every school cafeteria I ever ate in, and this is that same messy sandwich all grown up and moved into a casserole dish. You get the sweet and tangy tomato sauce, the browned meat, the soft peppers and onion, and then instead of a bun that dissolves in your hands halfway through, you get golden biscuits baked right on top. It is comfort food, plain and simple.

Here is the part that makes it fit the plan. We build it on ground turkey, so a single serving lands at {{protein}} grams of protein and {{cal}} calories. That is a real dinner, not a sad little diet plate, and it feeds fourteen containers out of one batch. Comfort food that still does the math in your favor is my kind of recipe.
prose.shop_smart:
Nothing on this list is exotic, which is exactly the point. Buy for the whole batch and you save yourself a second trip.

  • Biscuits: the build wants 21, and refrigerated biscuits come in 8-count cans, so grab about three cans. That leaves you a couple of biscuits to spare, which is not a tragedy.
  • Tomato sauce: you need 5 1/2 cups. Three standard 15-ounce cans cover it. Buy the no salt added kind if the shelf has it, since you are already salting to taste.
  • Ketchup: 1 1/2 cups comes out of a single regular bottle with plenty left for the fries later.
  • Shredded cheddar: the build uses about a pound and change, so one two-pound bag covers it with some to spare. Buy a block and shred it yourself if you like the meltier texture, but the bag works fine.
  • Ground turkey: 4 2/3 pounds. Watch for the bigger family packs or the value rolls, which is where the sensible pricing lives.
  • Bell peppers: nine total, about half red and half green. Whatever colors are cheapest that day will taste the same once they are cooked down.
prose.make_it:
This is a big batch, so ignore the fantasy of doing it all in one little skillet. Reach for your largest oven-safe pot or a roasting pan, and have a big baking dish ready for the finish.

  1. Make the sauce first. Preheat the oven to 375 degrees. In a bowl, whisk together the tomato sauce, ketchup, brown sugar, apple cider vinegar, Worcestershire sauce, onion powder, black pepper, and salt. Set it aside so the flavors get acquainted.
  2. Build the base. Heat your large pan over medium-high. If the pan looks dry, add a little cooking oil, though the turkey will bring plenty of its own fat in a minute. Add the minced garlic and cook about a minute until fragrant, then add the diced onion and the tomato paste. Cook one to two minutes so the paste browns a little and loses that raw edge. Add the diced bell peppers and cook three to five minutes to soften.
  3. Brown the turkey. Push the vegetables to the side and add the ground turkey. Let it sear undisturbed for two to three minutes, then break it into chunks and cook until it is browned through and reads 165 degrees inside.
  4. Bring it together. Drop the heat to medium-low, pour in the sauce, and stir everything to combine. Let it simmer five to six minutes so it thickens up slightly.
  5. Cap it and bake. Spread the mixture into your baking dish if you moved it out of the pan, then sprinkle the shredded cheddar over the top. Peel each biscuit at the center to make two thinner rounds and arrange them across the surface. Bake 15 to 20 minutes, until the biscuits are golden and cooked all the way through.
prose.portion_html:
Fourteen containers, and we portion by weight so nobody gets shorted. Weigh your empty pan before you cook if you can, then weigh it full at the end and subtract, or just tip the whole finished casserole onto a scale. Take that total, divide by fourteen, and that number is what goes in each container. A scale settles every argument at the dinner table.

The biscuits make it easy to eyeball too. You halved 21 biscuits into 42 thinner rounds, so that is three pieces per container with a little topping left to sort out. Spoon the sloppy joe base in first, set the biscuit pieces on top, and every box comes out to the same {{protein}} grams of protein and {{cal}} calories.
prose.cost_closing_html: Here is the whole reason we cook like this. Ground turkey, canned tomato sauce, a bag of cheese, and a few cans of biscuits are not premium groceries, and when you split one batch across fourteen containers, dinner lands at about ${{cost_ps}} a serving. That is a plate of real comfort food, {{protein}} grams of protein and all, for less than most people spend on a coffee.

head.description: One-Pan Sloppy Joe Casserole for meal prep: sweet-tangy ground turkey with peppers under golden biscuits, 45 g protein a serving, 14 budget containers.

steps: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees. Whisk together the tomato sauce, ketchup, brown sugar, apple cider vinegar, Worcestershire sauce, onion powder, black pepper, and salt in a bowl and set aside.

Heat a large oven-safe pan over medium-high, adding a little oil only if the pan looks dry. Add the minced garlic and cook about 1 minute until fragrant, then add the diced onion and tomato paste and cook 1 to 2 minutes to brown the paste.
Add the diced bell peppers and cook 3 to 5 minutes until softened.
Push the vegetables aside and add the ground turkey. Sear 2 to 3 minutes, then break it into pieces and cook until browned and 165 degrees throughout.
Reduce heat to medium-low, pour in the sauce, and stir to combine. Simmer 5 to 6 minutes until slightly thickened.
Sprinkle the shredded cheddar over the top. Halve each biscuit into two thinner rounds and arrange them over the mixture.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes until the biscuits are golden and cooked through, then portion across 14 containers.
